```{r setup, include = FALSE}
                      fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4, fig.retina = 2)

library(TRexSelector)
old_threads <- trex_set_num_threads(min(2L, trex_get_max_threads()))
```

# Sparse loadings with a guarantee

Principal component analysis (PCA) finds the directions of largest variance, and every variable
contributes to every loading vector. Sparse PCA asks for loadings with few non-zero entries, so that a
component can be read as a small set of variables. The T-Rex sparse PCA (T-Rex SPCA)
[@machkour2024spca] decides which variables enter a loading vector with the T-Rex selector. For each of
the $M$ components, ordinary PCA gives the component as a response, the T-Rex selector selects the
variables for it at the target false discovery rate (FDR), and a sparse loading vector is assembled
from the selected set. The selected set of every component is FDR-controlled.

# Data with two sparse factors

Two latent factors, the first loading on variables 1 to 10 and the second on variables 31 to 40, plus
noise.

```{r data}
set.seed(77)
n <- 200
p <- 60
Z <- matrix(rnorm(n * 2), n, 2)
V <- matrix(0, p, 2)
V[1:10, 1] <- 1 / sqrt(10)
V[31:40, 2] <- 1 / sqrt(10)
X <- 6 * Z[, 1] %*% t(V[, 1]) + 3 * Z[, 2] %*% t(V[, 2]) + matrix(rnorm(n * p), n, p)
```

# Running the selector

`TRexSPCASelector$new(X, M, tFDR, control, seed, verbose)` extracts `M` components. The elastic-net
penalty of the inner selector is chosen by cross-validation by default. `X` is centered in place during
`select()` and restored on return.

```{r run}
spca <- TRexSPCASelector$new(X, M = 2, tFDR = 0.1, seed = 9, verbose = FALSE,
                             control = trex_spca_control(K = 10))
spca$select()
spca$active_sets
```

The results are the scores `Z` ($n \times M$), the sparse loadings `V` ($p \times M$), the selected
sets, and the explained variance.

```{r fields}
dim(spca$Z)
dim(spca$V)
round(spca$adjusted_ev, 3)
round(spca$cumulative_ev, 3)
```

```{r loadings}
#| fig.width: 8.5
#| fig.height: 3.2
#| fig.cap: "The two sparse loading vectors. The true supports are variables 1 to 10 and 31 to 40."
library(ggplot2)
loadings <- data.frame(variable = rep(seq_len(p), 2), loading = c(spca$V[, 1], spca$V[, 2]),
                       component = rep(c("loading 1", "loading 2"), each = p))
on_support <- (loadings$component == "loading 1" & loadings$variable %in% 1:10) |
  (loadings$component == "loading 2" & loadings$variable %in% 31:40)
loadings$kind <- ifelse(on_support, "true support", "other")
ggplot(loadings, aes(variable, loading, colour = kind)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_segment(aes(xend = variable, yend = 0), linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ component) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("true support" = "#336C68", "other" = "#D1495B")) +
  labs(x = "Variable", y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "grey60"))
```

Sparse components are not orthogonal in general, so the explained variance is adjusted for the
non-orthogonality by a QR decomposition of the scores. `adjusted_ev` is the marginal share per
component and `cumulative_ev` the cumulative percentage.

# The control

`trex_spca_control()` sets the inner machinery.

- `mode`: `"ActiveSet"` (default) assembles the loading by a ridge regression of the component on the
  selected variables with penalty `lambda2_ridge_loadings`, `"Thresholded"` keeps the top $|A|$
  ordinary loadings and normalizes them.
- `lambda_2` and `lambda2_method`: the elastic-net penalty of the inner group selector, fixed or chosen
  by ridge cross-validation (`"CV_1SE_CCD"` by default when `lambda_2 < 0`). A value of 0 is the
  degenerate lasso case and gives a warning.
- `en_solver`: `"TENET_AUG"` (default) or `"TENET"`, two forms of the same elastic net.
- `K` and `max_dummy_multiplier`: the random experiments and the dummy cap of the inner selector.

T-Rex SPCA is defined on the elastic net, and `gvs_type = "IEN"` is rejected.

```{r thresholded}
thr <- TRexSPCASelector$new(X, M = 2, tFDR = 0.1, seed = 9, verbose = FALSE,
                            control = trex_spca_control(mode = "Thresholded", K = 10))
thr$select()
thr$active_sets
round(thr$cumulative_ev, 3)
```

# Memory-mapped data

`X` may be a memory-mapped matrix opened in `"readwrite"` mode (see the memory-mapping page). It is
centered in the file during `select()` and restored.

# Examples

The [TRexSelector_Examples](https://github.com/trexselector/TRexSelector_Examples/tree/main)
repository holds runnable demos and Monte Carlo studies of T-Rex SPCA, with their results and a
README per demo, in
[R](https://github.com/trexselector/TRexSelector_Examples/tree/main/R/trex_selector_methods/ad/trex_spca),
[Python](https://github.com/trexselector/TRexSelector_Examples/tree/main/Python/trex_selector_methods/ad/trex_spca)
and
[C++](https://github.com/trexselector/TRexSelector_Examples/tree/main/cpp/trex_selector_methods/ad/trex_spca).
